_changelog.changes: Added Mumbai DCPR 2034 + Delhi MPD-2021 (Session C)
Added Bangalore BBMP/UDD-2026, Pune UDCPR-2020, Hyderabad GHMC G.O.168 (Session D). All 6 launch cities now have real DCRs.

S54-004 fix: Chennai detached tier_50_to_150sqm side_right_m was incorrectly 0.0m (semi-detached/CBA behavior leaked into detached rules). Corrected to 0.7m, symmetric with side_left_m, per TNCDBR 2019 Schedule II.

detached._description: Standalone plot with setbacks on all 4 sides.

tiers._notes: Very small plots. Continuous Building Area may apply if declared — front = 0 if CBA, else 0.9m minimum.

Small plots (up to 30×40 ft). 0.7m setback on both sides per TNCDBR 2019 Schedule II. S54-004 fix (May 2026): side_right was incorrectly 0.0m (semi-detached/CBA behavior incorrectly applied to detached plots); now symmetric 0.7m matching side_left.
Medium plots. Full 4-side setbacks. Height ≤ 9m.
Larger plots, up to G+2. Road-width dependent front setback in real DCR — we use conservative 1.5m.
Larger plots, G+3. Road width ≥ 9m required. If road < 9m, revert to lower tier.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0 setback.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: Plot.shared_side (LEFT or RIGHT) determines which side is zeroed.

continuous._description: Row-house or Continuous Building Area (CBA) declared by local body per TNCDBR s.35(1) Explanation 1(v).
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front setback per road width. Rear setback minimum 1m.
continuous._notes: Rear 1m required for internal passage + fire access per TNCDBR CBA rule.

_fallback_nbc._authority: NBC 2016 Part 3 (general — city DCR pending in v0.2)
_fallback_nbc._disclosure_text: Using NBC 2016 general guidelines. Actual city DCR rules may differ — verify with your city's municipal corporation before applying for permit.

detached._description: NBC conservative defaults. All sides fully set back.

tiers._notes: Conservative defaults per NBC 2016 Part 3. Actual DCR may allow less.

semi_detached._description: Shared side = 0, other three per DETACHED.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED NBC tier, zero out shared side.

mumbai._reference_clause: DCPR 2034 — Front Open Spaces (residential) + Open Spaces general
mumbai._disclosure_text: DCPR 2034 distinguishes Mumbai Island City from Suburbs (different front setbacks). v0.9 defaults to SUBURBS values — most Mumbai homebuilders are outside Island City. If your plot is in Island City (south of Mahim/Sion), the rules differ. v1.0 will add a zone selector. For special roads (Pedder, Carmichael, Altamount, Napeansea, Hughes), front setback is 4.5m for both R and C — those are Island City-specific and not modelled here.

detached._description: Suburbs-default residential plotted housing. Front setback per DCPR 2034 Criteria 1 (road width). Side setback 1.5-2m per general open-space norms for low-rise residential.

tiers._notes: Suburbs, road width < 21m: front 4.5m for residential. Source: DCPR 2034 Criteria 1. Sides 1.5m for fire access and general open-space norms.
Medium plots in Suburbs. Side increased to 2.0m for G+1/G+2. Source: DCPR 2034 + general open spaces rule.
Suburbs, road width 21-52m: front 6.0m. Source: DCPR 2034 Criteria 1. Sides 3m for taller buildings.
Highway / road > 52m: front 7.5m (both Island and Suburbs). Source: DCPR 2034 Criteria 1.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0 setback.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: Plot.shared_side (LEFT or RIGHT) determines which side is zeroed. Mumbai DCPR allows this for cluster developments and certain cessed-building redevelopment cases.

continuous._description: Row-house pattern. DCPR 2034 generally requires open spaces, but for declared row-house schemes (e.g., MHADA layouts) side setbacks may be 0 with rear retained for fire access.
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front per road width. Rear 1.5m minimum.
continuous._notes: Row housing in Mumbai is uncommon outside MHADA/cluster schemes. These values are conservative reads of DCPR 2034 + IS 7290 row-house norms. Verify with MCGM building permission cell.

delhi._disclosure_text: Delhi setback values are best-available reads from MPD-2021 Clause 4.4.3 schedule and DDA Handbook. The exact printed table uses 'preceding category may be allowed' fallback if coverage isn't achievable — we use conservative reads. Verify with DDA or MCD building permission cell before construction. Max height 15m for all residential. Stilt mandatory 100-1000 sqm.

detached._description: Bungalow-pattern plotted housing. Plots ≤250 sqm follow row housing (no side setbacks). Plots >250 sqm are bungalow type with setback all around. Max height 15m.

tiers._notes: MPD-2021 minimum plot 32 sqm (EWS schemes lower). Row housing pattern, no setbacks required. Min 3 DUs.
Row housing pattern. 2m × 2m open courtyard required for new construction (MPD-2021 Note (b) under 4.4.3).
Row housing — front and rear only. Stilt mandatory in this range. Conservative read of MPD-2021 schedule.
Bungalow type begins at 250 sqm — setback all around. Stilt still mandatory.
Larger bungalow. Stilt mandatory upper limit (1000 sqm).
Large plot, often at edge of group housing scale. Stilt no longer mandatory; check fire access.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: Common in DDA cooperative housing societies. Plot.shared_side (LEFT or RIGHT) determines which side is zeroed.

continuous._description: Row housing pattern — explicitly allowed in MPD-2021 for plots ≤250 sqm. No side setbacks; front + rear only.
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front per road width. Rear 1m minimum.
continuous._notes: Row housing is the default pattern for plots ≤250 sqm in Delhi DDA areas. Minimum 3 DUs per row. Min plot 32 sqm.

bangalore._reference_clause: BBMP Building Bye-laws + UDD Nov 2025 simplified setbacks
bangalore._disclosure_text: Bangalore setback values reflect Karnataka UDD November 2025 amendments simplifying small-plot rules: plots ≤150 sqm now use fixed setbacks (0.6-0.9m) instead of percentage of dimensions. For plots >150 sqm, BBMP uses percentage-based formulas (typically 12%/8% of depth/width); we use conservative absolute values from the 2026 guide. Max height 12m for plots ≤150 sqm (excluding stilt). Verify with BBMP/BDA before construction as ward-specific rules may apply.

detached._description: BBMP residential plotted housing under simplified 2026 rules. Small plots have fixed setbacks; medium plots use percentage calculations approximated below; large plots (>4000 sqm) need 5m all sides.

tiers._notes: 20×30 ft typical. UDD 2026 fixed setbacks. Source: NewsFirstPrime UDD draft Nov 13 2025.
30×40 to 30×50 ft typical. Max height 12m (excluding stilt). UDD 2026 simplified rules.
BBMP rule: 12% depth front, 8% depth rear, 8% width sides. For 30×40 ft plot (~111 sqm): ~1.46m front, ~0.97m rear, ~0.74m sides. We use 1.5m as conservative rounded floor for plots in this range.
Larger plots scale up. BBMP percentage formulas give approximately these values. Source: WeBuildd BBMP byelaws guide.
Plots >4000 sqm: BBMP mandates 5m all sides. Source: RPRealtyPlus Karnataka amendments 2025.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0 setback.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: Plot.shared_side (LEFT or RIGHT) determines which side is zeroed. Common in BDA layouts and DDA-style cooperative housing in Bangalore.

continuous._description: Row housing — 'Row House' building type per BBMP byelaws. No side setbacks; front per road width; rear retained.
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front per road width. Rear 1m minimum.
continuous._notes: Row housing common in older BDA layouts and CITB schemes. BBMP requires front setback to scale with road width.

pune._reference_clause: UDCPR Table 6 — Marginal distances for residential ≤15m height
pune._disclosure_text: Pune setbacks reflect UDCPR (Unified DCPR) 2020 — applies statewide to Maharashtra municipal areas. PMC and PMRDA both follow UDCPR. v0.9 defaults to NON-CONGESTED area values (modern Pune layouts where most homebuilders are). Congested area (old city core) has reduced setbacks 1-1.5m. For buildings >15m height add +1m to all sides; for >24m use H/4 minimum 3m. Stilt height max 3m. Verify with PMC building permission cell.

detached._description: UDCPR residential plotted (height ≤15m, non-congested area). Front setback by road width per Table 6; sides/rear by plot size.

tiers._notes: UDCPR Table 6 small plot tier. For roads 6-12m wide front 1.5m, sides 1.0m. Source: Slideshare Pune Bye Laws + UDCPR Table 6.
Standard suburban Pune residential. Sides+rear 1.5m, front 1.5m for 6-12m roads. UDCPR Table 6 row.
Larger residential plot. UDCPR side margin scales up with plot area; rear 2m typical.
UDCPR for plots >500 sqm typically requires 3m sides and rear. Front 2.25m for 18m+ roads.
Large plots — typically group housing scope. Front scales with building height for >15m structures.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0 setback.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: UDCPR explicitly allows semi-detached buildings (Table 6 note 3). Side margin required on one side only (the non-shared side).

continuous._description: Row housing per UDCPR. No side setbacks; front per road width.
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front per road width. Rear 1.5m minimum.
continuous._notes: UDCPR row housing pattern. Common in PMC older townships and newer planned developments. Junction plots need larger setback.

hyderabad._reference_clause: G.O. Ms. No. 168 (2012) Table-III — Non-high-rise residential (buildings below 18m including stilt)
hyderabad._disclosure_text: Hyderabad setbacks reflect Telangana Building Rules G.O. Ms. 168 (2012) Table-III for non-high-rise residential (≤18m including stilt). HMDA and GHMC both apply this. For high-rise (>18m) different table applies; minimum 7m all sides for fire access. v0.9 covers G+1/G+2/G+3 residential which falls under the non-high-rise table. Front setback may also be governed by road width (separate building line rule). For final permit, use TS-bPASS portal with sanctioned setbacks. Verify with GHMC.

detached._description: GHMC/HMDA residential plotted (buildings ≤18m height inclusive of stilt). G.O. Ms. 168 Table-III tiers.

tiers._notes: G.O. 168 Table-III smallest residential tier. Front actually min(1.5m, 5% of plot width); we use 1.5m absolute floor as conservative read.
100-300 sqm typical Hyderabad residential. G.O. 168 Table-III standard tier.
Medium plot tier. Sides+rear 2m standard.
Larger residential. G.O. 168 Table-III scales setbacks up with plot area.
G.O. 168 — uniform 3m all sides for plots in this range.
Plots >1000 sqm: front 4.5m. For high-rise (>18m) fire access requires 7m all sides — not modelled here since v0.9 targets G+1/G+2/G+3.

semi_detached._description: Plot shares one side wall with a neighbour. Shared side = 0 setback.
semi_detached._rule: Use DETACHED tier setbacks, then zero out the shared side.
semi_detached._notes: Common in older Hyderabad townships (Banjara Hills, Jubilee Hills) and HMDA cooperative housing. Plot.shared_side determines which side is zeroed.

continuous._description: Row housing — 'Row Housing' permitted under HMDA layout rules. No side setbacks; front per road width; rear retained.
continuous._rule: No side setbacks. Front per road width. Rear 1.5m minimum.
continuous._notes: Row housing common in HMDA-approved layouts. Front building line scales with road width per HMDA amendments.
